episodes.title: Set up Agent HQ
episodes.subtitle: Connect a model, fill every role, open a project
intro: Episode one: setting up Agent HQ.
In three short steps, you'll connect a model, give every role a model, and open your project.

cues.text: This is Agent HQ on first launch. Sovereign's chat says it needs a model first, so let's connect one.
Open Connections, then click Connect provider.
Choose the company whose models you want. We'll pick Anthropic.
Choose Signed-in CLI. If you already pay for Claude Code, Agent HQ uses that subscription. No API key.
Agent HQ checks that the tool is installed and signed in, and lists its models.
Save the connection, and Anthropic shows as connected.
Local tools lists what's on this computer. A missing tool gets an Install button, and a command you can copy.
Next, open Role defaults. Every role needs a model before the team can work.
Click Fill empty roles. Each role gets a strong starting model, and you can change any of them later.
Now open your project. Click the project switcher at the top of the sidebar.
Select the folder, then click Open. Agents can only read, write and run commands inside it.
This is the Workspace: files on the left, the editor and terminal in the middle, and Sovereign on the right.
The warning is gone. Sovereign has a model, and it's ready for your first task.

outro: Setup is done. You connected a provider, filled every role, and opened a project.
Next, run your first task in Manual mode.
recap: Connected Anthropic through its signed-in CLI

episodes.title: Manual mode
episodes.subtitle: Approve the plan, then decide on every file
intro: You approve the plan, then decide on every file yourself. It's the default, and the safest way to start.

cues.text: Under the chat, Approval says Ask every time. That's Manual mode.
Switch to Plan, so Sovereign proposes the work and waits for you.
Describe the change in plain words.
And send it.
Sovereign replies with a plan: three tasks, and the agent for each one.
Every task is rated simple, standard or complex, and runs on a model picked for that level.
For the helper, Sovereign chose GPT-5 Codex instead, and tells you why.
The documentation task waits for the other two to finish.
Nothing runs until you click Approve and run.
Pulse and Titan work at the same time. Follow them on the Tasks board.
When they're done, Sentinel, the QA agent, reviews all of the work.
Back in the Workspace, Sovereign reports that QA approved the run.
In Manual mode, nothing is written yet. Open Changes: every file is a pending proposal.
Click Diff to compare a proposal with the file on disk.
Looks good? Click Apply, and the file is written to your project.
It's marked applied, and git now lists the file as modified.
Changed your mind? Undo puts the original file back.
Apply the other files the same way, or discard the ones you don't want.

outro: In Manual mode, you approved the plan, and decided on every file.
Next, let the team write files on its own, with Auto mode.
recap: Planned with Sovereign before anything ran
Approved the plan and watched the team
Compared, applied, undid and discarded each file

episodes.title: Auto-apply and Full access
episodes.subtitle: Let the team write files, or start work on its own
episodes.file: 03 - Auto mode - auto-apply and full access
intro: Episode three: Auto-apply and Full access.
When you trust the team, let it write files for you, or even start work without asking.

cues.text: Open the Approval menu under the chat. There are three modes.
Choose Auto-apply changes.
Agent HQ explains exactly what changes, and asks once. Turn on auto-apply.
Now ask for a change in Plan mode, as before.
You still approve the plan.
Once Sentinel approves, the files are written automatically. No Apply clicks.
In Changes, each file is marked auto, and applied.
Full access goes one step further. Pick it from the same menu.
It starts work as soon as Sovereign has a plan, so read the warning, then allow it.
Switch to Build, and describe the next change.
Send it. This time there is no approval step.
Sovereign plans, the team builds, Sentinel reviews, and the files are written.
Check it in the terminal. The file really changed on disk.
Every auto-applied file can still be undone, from Changes.
Switch back to Ask every time whenever you want to review again. Going back never asks.

outro: Auto-apply writes approved files for you. Full access also starts work without waiting.
Next: how Agent HQ picks a model for every task, and how you take control.
recap: Turned on Auto-apply: QA-approved files are written for you
Allowed Full access: Build requests run without approval
Checked the result on disk and undid a change

episodes.title: Models and routing
episodes.subtitle: Automatic by default, yours to pin, lock or force
intro: Episode four: which model does each agent use?
By default, it's automatic. Here's how Agent HQ decides, and every way to take control.

cues.text: Open Settings, then Models and routing.
This card shows who decides, from your strictest setting down to fully automatic.
Sovereign rates every task simple, standard or complex, and each level runs on its own model.
Auto picks the strongest model for each level, across every provider you've connected. Simple work doesn't spend your best model.
Take turns means two equally good models share the work, so both subscriptions last longer.
To choose yourself, pick a model for a level. Here, Claude Opus 5.5 for complex work.
Preferred is a starting point that Sovereign may change. Locked means always this model.
Force my setup makes every pin and locked agent apply exactly, with no exceptions.
We'll leave it off, so the AI stays dynamic.
You can also lock one agent. Open Agents, and configure Titan.
Give Titan a model, and choose Always this model. Titan now ignores the levels.
With the Magpie gateway, Agent HQ can also let Magpie pick which subscription serves each call.
Your levels become Magpie groups, routed by the quota you have left. Codex is down to seven percent this week, so it gets less work.
The ranking explains every choice: the model's size, whether a newer version exists, and how it did on your real tasks.
And the decisions log records which model ran each task, and why.

outro: Models are automatic by default, and every level, agent and account can be pinned, locked or forced.
Next: a team that grows and learns with your project.
recap: Each task runs on the best model for its level
Pinned a level, and locked one agent
Let Magpie spread work by quota, and read the ranking

episodes.title: A team that grows
episodes.subtitle: New specialists, mentors for juniors, lasting memory
intro: Episode five: a team that grows with your project.
Sovereign hires the specialists a task needs, juniors report to a senior, and every agent remembers what it learns.

cues.text: With Team set to Sovereign designs the team, Sovereign decides how many agents each request needs.
Let's ask for work that no current agent specializes in.
Sovereign proposes two new agents: Vera, a testing lead, and Kit, a junior who reports to her.
Each new agent comes with a role, a model, and a reason.
Approve, and the new agents join the team and start working.
Kit is a junior, so Vera reviews Kit's work first. That's the N plus one review, before QA.
In the Agents graph, every junior is linked to the senior who mentors it.
You can hire too. Click Onboard junior.
Pick a specialty, and a matching mentor is suggested. For QA, that's Sentinel.
Give the junior a name, and click Onboard.
Agents keep lessons from QA feedback, mentor reviews, and what you teach them. Open Growth to see them.
Each card shows the agent's level, its focus areas, and the last thing it learned.
To teach the whole team, type slash remember in the chat.

outro: Your team grows with every project: new specialists, mentors for juniors, and memory that carries over.
Last episode: the workspace tools you'll use every day.
recap: Sovereign hired a lead and a junior for the task
The junior's work was reviewed by its mentor
Onboarded a junior and taught the team a lesson

episodes.title: The workspace
episodes.subtitle: Files, search, Ask mode, terminal and reports
intro: Files and search, Ask mode, a real terminal, and the reports that show what the team did.

cues.text: The explorer shows your project. Click a file, and it opens in a tab.
Edit it like any code editor. Control S saves it to disk.
Press Control K to jump to any file or command.
Ask mode is for questions. Sovereign reads the project and answers, but never changes files.
The terminal is a real shell, opened in your project folder.
Click plus for another shell. Each one is a separate tab.
The Activity panel logs every step the team takes, so nothing happens out of sight.
And Reports shows runs, tokens and estimated cost, for every agent and model.

outro: That's the workspace: files, search, Ask mode, a real terminal, and reports.
You've seen the whole series. Open Agent HQ, and give your team its first task.
recap: Opened, edited and saved a file
Searched with Control K and asked about the code
Used the terminal, Activity and Reports
